I'm not physicist so I might be wrong, but I don't think the other answers are correct. In fact, I think that if the speed of light suddenly got 100 times higher, absolutely nothing would change .
items.original_question: 如果光速提高 100 倍会怎样？想象一下，光速是我们宇宙中光速的 100 倍。来自月球的光大约需要 1/100 秒，太阳光到达我们的眼睛大约需要 4 秒，来自附近的半人马座阿尔法星大约需要 16 天，来自银河系中心大约需要 260 年。假设相对论放大到 $c$ 的更高值，这会让前往其他世界变得更容易吗？除了很棒之外，我还应该记住其他重要的考虑因素吗？编辑：根据前几个回复，如果可能的话，我想假设宇宙不会严重燃烧的场景。但也许如此快速的因果关系传播让我没有出路......

rubrics.question_focus: What If the Speed of Light Were 100 Times Faster?

criteria.name: Counterfactual Premise Fidelity and Assumption Control
criteria.criteria_description: Evaluates whether the response clearly specifies what is held constant (e.g., physical constants, unit systems, spacetime structure) when the speed of light is 100× larger, and consistently reasons under that explicit counterfactual without drifting back to real-world physics.
criteria.1-2: Ignores the need to specify what else changes; reasoning mixes real-world constants inconsistently.
criteria.3-4: Mentions that other constants matter but does not clearly fix assumptions; inconsistent application of the premise.
criteria.5-6: States at least one key assumption (e.g., other constants fixed) but applies it unevenly or incompletely.
criteria.7-8: Clearly specifies what is held constant (e.g., G, ħ, charge, units) and mostly reasons consistently under that setup.
criteria.9-10: Explicitly frames multiple possible interpretations (e.g., dimensionless constants vs unit change), selects one, and maintains strict logical consistency throughout.

criteria.name: Core Physical Mechanism Analysis
criteria.criteria_description: Assesses depth and correctness of mechanisms linking a 100× larger speed of light to changes in relativity, electromagnetism, atomic structure, or dimensionless constants (e.g., fine-structure constant).
criteria.1-2: Provides speculative or superficial claims with no physical mechanism.
criteria.3-4: Mentions relativity or energy formulas but with major misconceptions or no causal linkage.
criteria.5-6: Correctly identifies at least one major mechanism (e.g., reduced relativistic effects, impact on E=mc²) but with limited depth.
criteria.7-8: Explains multiple mechanisms (e.g., Lorentz factor scaling, mass–energy relation, atomic spectra via α) with mostly correct causal reasoning.
criteria.9-10: Accurately connects changes in c to relativistic dynamics, field propagation, and dimensionless constants, distinguishing which physical effects would materially change and why.

criteria.name: Long-Range Downstream Consequence Coverage
criteria.criteria_description: Evaluates how well the response traces extended causal chains from fundamental physics to astrophysics, cosmology, technology, or everyday experience.
criteria.1-2: Focuses on a single isolated effect with no broader implications.
criteria.3-4: Mentions a few downstream domains (e.g., space travel, communication) without causal development.
criteria.5-6: Develops at least one extended chain (e.g., altered stellar processes → star lifetimes) but omits other major domains.
criteria.7-8: Covers multiple domains (e.g., particle physics, stellar structure, cosmology, human-scale effects) with coherent causal links.
criteria.9-10: Provides a well-structured, multi-domain cascade from microphysics to cosmic and experiential consequences, showing how changes propagate across scales.

criteria.name: Contradiction Control and Internal Coherence
criteria.criteria_description: Measures whether the reasoning avoids internal contradictions (e.g., claiming both massive and negligible change under the same assumptions) and maintains logical continuity over long chains of inference.
criteria.1-2: Contains clear contradictions or mutually incompatible claims.
criteria.3-4: Shows tension between claims (e.g., says “nothing changes” but lists major effects) without reconciliation.
criteria.5-6: Mostly coherent but with minor inconsistencies or unstated assumption shifts.
criteria.7-8: Logically consistent with only subtle gaps; assumptions remain stable across sections.
criteria.9-10: Fully coherent; apparent paradoxes (e.g., unit redefinitions vs physical change) are explicitly resolved.

criteria.name: Uncertainty Calibration and Interpretation Sensitivity
criteria.criteria_description: Assesses whether the response acknowledges ambiguity in how the counterfactual is defined (e.g., change in dimensional constant vs change in dimensionless constants) and calibrates confidence accordingly.
criteria.1-2: Expresses unwarranted certainty with no recognition of ambiguity.
criteria.3-4: Briefly notes uncertainty but does not integrate it into reasoning.
criteria.5-6: Recognizes at least one ambiguity and partially conditions conclusions on it.
criteria.7-8: Clearly distinguishes alternative interpretations and explains how outcomes differ under each.
criteria.9-10: Systematically analyzes multiple interpretations, compares their implications, and proportionally calibrates conclusions and confidence.

items.question: What If Humans Were Placed on an Oxygen-Bearing Planet with a Different Atmosphere?
human_answers: There are three separate issues here: Too much oxygen, and the human body (as well as any other organic material) will be highly flammable. You don't really want to live there.
100% oxygen is dangerous - stuff will burn, oxygenation can damage tissues. Apollo 1 had pure oxygen atmosphere, did not ended up well.
100% O 2 At normal atmospherical pressure ( 101.325 kPa ) if your only gas is O 2 you will have a partial pressure of 101.325 kPa of O 2 ... lethal, deadly and painful.
10% is too little and wouldn't work. If you increased it to 20%: 100% oxygen: I think we'd spontaneously combust...this is toxic as well.
items.original_question: 如果我们把人类放在大气层与地球大气层不同但仍含有氧气的行星上，人类能够呼吸吗？来自维基百科：按体积计算，干燥空气含有 78.09% 氮气、20.95% 氧气、0.93% 氩气、0.039% 二氧化碳和少量其他气体。例如，人类能够在这样的大气中生存吗？ ： 100% 氧气，无其他 10% 氧气，90% 氮气 10% 氧气，90% 氩气 10% 氧气，90% 二氧化碳 10% 氧气，90% 氦气 10% 氧气，90% 氙气 2% 氧气，98% 其他无毒元素

rubrics.question_focus: What If Humans Were Placed on an Oxygen-Bearing Planet with a Different Atmosphere?

criteria.name: Counterfactual Premise Fidelity
criteria.criteria_description: Evaluates whether the response consistently reasons under the specific counterfactual: humans placed on an oxygen-bearing planet with a different atmospheric composition (e.g., higher O2 fraction, different pressure, or additional gases), without reverting to Earth-normal assumptions.
criteria.1-2: Ignores or misinterprets the premise; assumes Earth-like atmosphere or discusses irrelevant scenarios.
criteria.3-4: Acknowledges atmospheric differences but largely defaults to Earth norms or introduces inconsistent assumptions.
criteria.5-6: Maintains the altered-atmosphere premise but with occasional unexamined Earth-based assumptions.
criteria.7-8: Consistently reasons within a clearly specified altered oxygen/atmospheric scenario.
criteria.9-10: Explicitly defines key atmospheric differences (e.g., O2 fraction, pressure, other gases) and rigorously maintains logical consistency throughout.

criteria.name: Physiological Mechanism Depth
criteria.criteria_description: Assesses explanation of biological mechanisms by which altered oxygen levels and atmospheric composition affect human physiology (e.g., oxygen toxicity, oxidative stress, pulmonary and CNS effects).
criteria.1-2: Provides vague claims (e.g., 'it would be bad') with no mechanisms.
criteria.3-4: Mentions one mechanism (e.g., oxygen toxicity) but with minimal explanation.
criteria.5-6: Explains basic mechanisms such as reactive oxygen species or pressure effects, but incompletely.
criteria.7-8: Clearly explains multiple mechanisms (e.g., CNS toxicity, lung damage, oxidative stress) and links them to atmospheric parameters.
criteria.9-10: Integrates detailed, causally accurate physiological pathways and distinguishes between concentration vs. partial pressure effects.

criteria.name: Long-Range Causal Chain Coherence
criteria.criteria_description: Evaluates how well the response traces downstream consequences over time, from immediate exposure effects to ecological, technological, or evolutionary implications.
criteria.1-2: Lists isolated effects with no causal linkage or temporal progression.
criteria.3-4: Describes short-term effects only, with weak or fragmented causal connections.
criteria.5-6: Connects short-term and some medium-term consequences but lacks depth or misses key transitions.
criteria.7-8: Provides a coherent chain from atmospheric properties to biological, environmental, and societal impacts.
criteria.9-10: Develops a multi-stage, tightly linked causal chain (e.g., flammability → infrastructure risk → ecological fire regimes → adaptation pressures) with clear temporal structure.

criteria.name: Coverage of Major Risk Domains
criteria.criteria_description: Measures whether the answer addresses the major consequence domains specific to high or altered oxygen atmospheres: flammability/combustion risk, human tissue toxicity, pressure effects, and interactions with other atmospheric gases.
criteria.1-2: Misses most major domains; focuses narrowly on one minor aspect.
criteria.3-4: Covers only one major domain (e.g., flammability) with limited acknowledgment of others.
criteria.5-6: Covers at least two major domains but omits or underdevelops others.
criteria.7-8: Addresses flammability, physiological toxicity, and at least one additional factor (pressure or other gases).
criteria.9-10: Comprehensively covers flammability, oxygen toxicity (with pressure sensitivity), material/chemical reactivity, and plausible atmospheric co-factor effects.

criteria.name: Uncertainty Calibration and Contradiction Control
criteria.criteria_description: Assesses whether the response appropriately qualifies claims (e.g., dependence on partial pressure, duration of exposure) and avoids internal contradictions.
criteria.1-2: Contains major contradictions or confidently states incorrect generalizations (e.g., 'any extra oxygen is instantly lethal').
criteria.3-4: Shows overgeneralization or minor inconsistencies without clarification.
criteria.5-6: Mostly consistent but lacks explicit qualification of key variables (e.g., pressure, exposure time).
criteria.7-8: Carefully qualifies outcomes based on pressure, concentration, and duration; internally consistent.
criteria.9-10: Explicitly distinguishes thresholds, short- vs long-term exposure, and clearly bounds uncertainty while maintaining full logical consistency.

items.question: How Could You Destroy a City so Thoroughly That Archaeologists 4,000 Years Later Would Misread the Cause?
human_answers: I have much academic experience with some of this, especially the second part of your question. I'll address a few different sides of things.

items.original_question: 如何彻底摧毁一座城市，而不为4000年后的人类留下任何线索？背景 我想彻底烧毁一座城市。一切不得残留，尘归尘，尘归尘。尽管我是一个超自然的存在，但我希望这一切以自然的方式发生。我还希望这次破坏不会留下任何痕迹，以便 4000 年后人类可以利用这些痕迹来确定到底发生了什么。然而，该事件可能会留下痕迹，让他们猜测发生了什么，但绝对不应该导致确切的原因。细节 完全烧毁一座城市（阅读：摧毁，但我喜欢火）。该市地处海拔以上，属半干旱气候。该事件可能不会留下任何线索。这意味着 4000 年后的人类无法准确识别发生了什么。然而，破坏可能会留下痕迹，让人们想知道到底发生了什么。主要的一点是，这座城市本身应该成为一个传说，也就是说，毁灭地点不应该留下任何可以证明被毁城市存在的痕迹。不过，如果人们知道发生了某种自然灾害也很好，但最好他们不确切知道是什么类型的自然灾害。 事件时间：公元前 2,000 年（大约）。销毁最好在 24 小时内发生。优选地，破坏方法可以摧毁主要用岩石和粘土类物质建造的城市。我有什么选择？有什么可以利用的自然灾害吗？这是否可能以自然的方式实现？请发挥创意。我本以为是“从天而降的火”，但陨石撞击的痕迹要持续 4000 多年。编辑 1：我删除了以下要求，以使更多答案成为可能：该区域不存在火山活动或地震活动。编辑2：答案和评论的数量非常多，谢谢！我重写了要求/细节，使事情更加清晰。我还在其中两个添加了“最好”一词，这意味着应该可以提供更多的答案。只要记住“最好”...还要注意，这个问题首先谈论两个城市。我将其更改为一个城市，因为：如果它适用于一个城市，那么它可能适用于任意数量的城市。
